title: Tip from Angela - Mixing Knowledge
summary: A short study tip: learning sticks better when topics from different modules are combined in small programs rather than practised only in isolation.

concepts.heading: Interleave topics to strengthen recall
points: Practising each topic only inside its own module builds weaker mental links than using several topics together.
Example pairing: conditionals (if/else) from one module with loops (for/while) from another.
Exercise to try: write a tiny program of roughly 5-10 lines that deliberately combines ideas from two different course modules, such as one from module 3 and one from module 5.
The program does not need to be impressive; the act of combining the ideas is what consolidates them.

gaps_and_ideas: (Extra) Possible 'mix-it-up' mini-challenges in the playground that require combining two earlier lessons, e.g. a loop that builds list items from an array with a conditional class.
